--- a/results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh
+++ b/results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh
@@ -1,431 +1,526 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # install.sh — the ONE deployment path for the operator tools (design full-speed-v2 §7).
 #
 # Operator scripts drive tmux, the crontab and the host process table, so they cannot be
 # run from the checkout (which is mid-merge for minutes at a time).  They are therefore
 # COPIED to ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/ by this installer and never edited on the
 # host: on 2026-09-12 three versions of the lane runner ran at once, `merge-daemon-v9h.sh`
 # called a `/tmp/merge-v2.sh` that does not exist, and the shim was patched by an
 # `assert old in s` here-doc against a 90-character substring.
 #
 # Usage:
 #   install.sh [--force] [--compat-tmp] [--crons] [--start-loops] [--dry-run]
 #   install.sh --verify                 # dependency/hash check (the merge daemon's gate)
 #   install.sh --record <name>          # re-record a regenerated file (run_mode.py set speed)
 #
 # Options:
 #   --force        overwrite a deployed copy whose hash matches no released version.
 #                  The previous copy is MOVED to owner-bin/attic/<ts>/, never deleted.
 #   --start-loops  start capacityd.sh (the 60 s capacity controller loop) if it is not
+#                  running, and fire one detached build-on-chsh.sh --seed-refresh (which
+#                  returns immediately unless the run is fast and lists chsh)
 #                  already running and no stop file holds it.  Without a running
 #                  controller nothing writes watchdog/max-codex-*, the caps stay frozen
 #                  at whatever seeded them, there is no AIMD, no 5xx trip and no
 #                  half-open probe — the 2026-09-12 situation, recovered by hand — and on
 #                  a fresh host lane.sh:wait_for_slot fails closed with
 #                  `no-capacity-record`.  The merge daemon and the goal keeper are NOT
 #                  started here: owner-resume.sh owns those (design §5).
 #   --compat-tmp   create /tmp/<name> SYMLINKS into owner-bin/ so anything still invoking
 #                  a historical /tmp path runs versioned code.  Nothing is ever written or
 #                  edited in /tmp; an existing regular file there is refused, not clobbered.
 #   --crons        run install-crons.sh afterwards (crontab regenerated from run-mode).
+#                  Also installs the chsh build farm's known-hosts file (below).
 #   --dry-run      print the plan and touch nothing (implies --dry-run for --crons too).
 #   --dest DIR     install into DIR instead of $MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin (tests).
 #   --compat-dir D create the compat symlinks in D instead of /tmp (tests).
 #   --speed S      render the PATH shim for speed S instead of asking run_mode.py (tests).
 #
 # What is written under owner-bin/:
 #   <tool>              the deployed copy, mode from the table below
 #   tools-version       describe= sha= short= installed_at= source= installer=  (one release)
 #   manifest.sha256     "<sha256>  <name>" for every file deployed now (sha256sum format)
 #   manifest.accepted   every hash this release accepts for a name; the PATH shim has two
 #                       (the fast and the default rendering), because run_mode.py set speed
 #                       regenerates it in place
 #   repo-root           the checkout this release was installed from
+#
+# Outside owner-bin/ this installer also places the chsh build farm's host keys at
+# $MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/chsh/known_hosts, copied only from the explicitly
+# trusted $MIPSTARRE_CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS or the durable copy under the cache root.  The
+# first install keeps its own copy at watchdog/chsh/known_hosts.source, and `--verify`
+# says so when the file is missing or empty instead of leaving the
+# absence of `host=chsh` rows as the only signal.  They are runtime
+# state, not a committed file, and build-on-chsh.sh uses them with
+# StrictHostKeyChecking=yes.  Without them the offload exits 64 and every lane simply
+# builds on ghz — a missing file is a warning here, never a failed install.
 #   attic/<ts>/         the previous copy of every file this run replaced, plus its manifest
 #
 # Refusal rule (the point of the installer): a deployed file whose hash is neither the
 # incoming one, nor the manifest row, nor an accepted variant, nor a hash recorded in an
 # attic manifest, is a HAND PATCH.  It is reported and the install stops with exit 4.
 # --force is the only way past, and it keeps the patch in the attic.
 #
 # Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 --verify found a missing file or a hash mismatch ·
 #             4 a hand patch was refused · 5 a required source file is missing
 set -euo pipefail
 
 PROG="install.sh"
 
-usage() { sed -n '2,52p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+usage() { sed -n '2,60p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
 
 FORCE=0; COMPAT=0; CRONS=0; DRY=0; VERIFY=0; RECORD=""; START_LOOPS=0
 DEST=""; SPEED=""; COMPAT_DIR="${MIPSTARRE_COMPAT_DIR:-/tmp}"
 while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
   case "$1" in
     --force) FORCE=1 ;;
     --compat-tmp) COMPAT=1 ;;
     --crons) CRONS=1 ;;
     --start-loops) START_LOOPS=1 ;;
     --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
     --verify) VERIFY=1 ;;
     --record) RECORD="${2:-}"; [ -n "$RECORD" ] || { echo "$PROG: --record needs a tool name" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
     --dest) DEST="${2:-}"; [ -n "$DEST" ] || { echo "$PROG: --dest needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
     --compat-dir) COMPAT_DIR="${2:-}"; [ -n "$COMPAT_DIR" ] || { echo "$PROG: --compat-dir needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
     --speed) SPEED="${2:-}"; [ -n "$SPEED" ] || { echo "$PROG: --speed needs fast or default" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
     -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
     *) echo "$PROG: unknown argument '$1'" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
   esac
   shift
 done
 
 CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
 DEST="${DEST:-$CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin}"
 TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
 
+CHSH_STATE="$CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/chsh"
+CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_SRC="${MIPSTARRE_CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS:-}"
+
+# A predictable shared /tmp path is never a trust source: another user could
+# pre-create it before the first install.  The first explicitly trusted copy is
+# retained under the cache root for later installs.
+CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_KEEP="$CHSH_STATE/known_hosts.source"
+
+chsh_known_hosts_source() { # the file to install from, or nothing
+  local candidate
+  for candidate in "$CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_SRC" "$CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_KEEP"; do
+    [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -s "$candidate" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$candidate"; return 0; }
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+install_chsh_known_hosts() {
+  local src
+  if ! src="$(chsh_known_hosts_source)"; then
+    echo "$PROG: no explicitly trusted chsh known-hosts and no durable copy at" \
+         "$CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_KEEP; the build farm stays unusable"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  mkdir -p "$CHSH_STATE"
+  if [ ! -r "$CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_KEEP" ] || ! cmp -s "$src" "$CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_KEEP"; then
+    cp "$src" "$CHSH_STATE/.known_hosts.keep.new"
+    chmod 600 "$CHSH_STATE/.known_hosts.keep.new"
+    mv "$CHSH_STATE/.known_hosts.keep.new" "$CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_KEEP"
+    echo "$PROG: chsh host keys kept at $CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_KEEP (from $src)"
+  fi
+  if [ -r "$CHSH_STATE/known_hosts" ] && cmp -s "$src" "$CHSH_STATE/known_hosts"; then
+    echo "$PROG: chsh known_hosts unchanged ($CHSH_STATE/known_hosts)"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  cp "$src" "$CHSH_STATE/.known_hosts.new"
+  chmod 644 "$CHSH_STATE/.known_hosts.new"
+  mv "$CHSH_STATE/.known_hosts.new" "$CHSH_STATE/known_hosts"
+  echo "$PROG: chsh known_hosts installed at $CHSH_STATE/known_hosts (from $src)"
+}
+
+# --verify reports the keys.  Never an exit-3 failure: a run that does not list
+# chsh does not need them, and a missing file costs build minutes and nothing
+# else.  What it must never be is invisible.
+verify_chsh_known_hosts() {
+  if [ -s "$CHSH_STATE/known_hosts" ]; then
+    printf '%s: chsh known_hosts present (%s bytes)\n' "$PROG" \
+      "$(wc -c < "$CHSH_STATE/known_hosts" | tr -d ' ')"
+    return 0
+  fi

 # and local/bin/ci.sh so the two carry ONE copy of the fallback rule.
 #
 #   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/offload-build.sh"
 #   offload_local_build() { ( cd "$W" && timeout 2700 lake build "$@" ); }

 #
 # The rule it exists to keep (local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md):
 #

 #     `run_mode.py get offload` through `build-on-chsh.sh --check`, never of a
 #     file or an environment variable of our own.
 #   * A LANE MUST NEVER FAIL BECAUSE CHSH IS UNREACHABLE.  Exit 64 (chsh
 #     unusable) and 65 (artifacts not returned) fall back to the local build;
 #     every other exit code is the build's own verdict and is passed through,
 #     because a proof that does not compile does not compile anywhere and a
 #     silent local retry would only spend the build lease twice.
 #   * Which host built is in the lane log and, whenever the offload was
 #     enabled, in $MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/chsh/offload.log.
 #
 # The caller defines `offload_local_build <targets ...>`, which runs the local
 # build exactly as it did before (cwd, timeout and git-env handling differ
 # between the two callers); without one, a plain `lake build` in the worktree

 #

 #   ever point at a DIFFERENT script, never turn the offload on — the run mode is
 #   asked here as well, so a script whose `--check` exits 0 still offloads
 #   nothing outside full speed mode), MIPSTARRE_OFFLOAD=0 (never offload, for a
 #   run that must stay on this host), MIPSTARRE_OFFLOAD_TIMEOUT_S (wall clock for
 #   one offload, default 3300; a timeout is a fallback, not a lane failure),
 #   MIPSTARRE_RUN_MODE, MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT, MIPSTARRE_OWNER_BIN,

 #: build on this host; ssh's ServerAlive only notices a link that is dead, not
 #: one that is merely slow.

 }
 
 offload_record() { # <line> — one row in watchdog/chsh/offload.log

   printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >> "$dir/offload.log" 2>/dev/null || true
 }

   owner="${MIPSTARRE_OWNER_BIN:-$cache/owner-bin}"
   checkout="${MIPSTARRE_CHECKOUT:-$HOME/MIPStarRE-qpbt}"
   for candidate in "${MIPSTARRE_OFFLOAD_SCRIPT:-}" \
                    "$owner/build-on-chsh.sh" \
                    "$checkout/results/telemetry/owner-tools/build-on-chsh.sh"; do
     [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -r "$candidate" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$candidate"; return 0; }
   done

 }

+    else
+      # A missing marker means the wrapper did not observe remote completion;

   fi

 # build-on-chsh.sh — offload one worktree's Lean build to the chsh build farm.
 #
 #   build-on-chsh.sh [--dry-run] <worktree-path> [lake targets ...]
 #   build-on-chsh.sh --check                  # is the offload enabled right now?

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# build-on-chsh.sh — offload one worktree's Lean build to the chsh build farm.
     3	#
     4	#   build-on-chsh.sh [--dry-run] <worktree-path> [lake targets ...]
     5	#   build-on-chsh.sh --check                  # is the offload enabled right now?
     6	#   build-on-chsh.sh [--dry-run] --seed-refresh
     7	#
     8	# Runs ON ghz.  chsh is a pure build node: 192 aarch64 cores, a byte-identical
     9	# copy of the Mathlib package cache, the same Lean toolchain and a hardlink
    10	# build seed, fed from ghz by rsync over the internal link (86.7 MB/s).
    11	#
    12	# THE OWNER'S RULE (local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md): chsh is used only in
    13	# full speed mode and never otherwise, and no codex session ever runs there.
    14	# The rule is enforced here as well as in the callers: without `--dry-run`
    15	# this script refuses to contact chsh unless `run_mode.py get offload` says
    16	# `yes`, which happens only when the run is fast, unpaused and lists the host.
    17	# An unreadable run mode is `no` — unknown is never "use the second host".
    18	#
    19	# What a build does:
    20	#   1. rsync the worktree's sources to chsh builds/<lane>/ (excluding .lake,
    21	#      .git, .worktrees and results/telemetry)
    22	#   2. seed <lane>/.lake/build from the DATA seed with `cp -al` (hardlinks, one
    23	#      filesystem, no data copied) and point <lane>/.lake/packages at the
    24	#      shared Mathlib cache
    25	#   3. run `lake build [targets]` in the lane on chsh
    26	#   4. rsync the WHOLE of .lake/build back into the worktree (Mathlib lives in
    27	#      .lake/packages and is never touched)
    28	#   5. exit with lake's exit code
    29	#
    30	# Step 4 returns the whole tree and not the delta ON PURPOSE.  Returning only
    31	# `find lib ir -newer .offload-stamp` returns what chsh rebuilt RELATIVE TO ITS
    32	# OWN SEED, and the two hosts' starting points are not the same object: chsh's
    33	# seed is refreshed after every merge and therefore tracks `main`, while a ghz
    34	# worktree is warmed from the hot-main snapshot, which lags it by hours.  Every
    35	# module that moved on main inside that gap has an olean in chsh's seed — not
    36	# rebuilt, not newer than the stamp, not returned — and NO olean on ghz.  The
    37	# build then "succeeds" with host=chsh, nothing falls back, and the lane dies
    38	# later at the pre-push per-file `lake env lean` gate, which needs those
    39	# imports' oleans on THIS host, or triggers an unbounded local rebuild outside
    40	# the machine-wide build lease it has already released.  rsync's own size/mtime
    41	# delta still transfers only what is missing, so the cost is one file-list walk;
    42	# the stamp survives only as the `artifacts=N` field in the log.
    43	#
    44	# Exit codes — the caller must be able to tell "chsh is unusable" from "the
    45	# proof does not compile", because the first falls back to a local build and
    46	# the second must not:
    47	#   0        the build succeeded on chsh and its artifacts are in the worktree
    48	#   64       chsh is UNUSABLE (offload disabled, missing known-hosts, ssh or
    49	#            rsync failure, lane busy, toolchain mismatch).  Build locally.
    50	#   65       the build ran but its artifacts could not be returned.  Build
    51	#            locally; the worktree may hold a partial set.
    52	#   2        usage error
    53	#   anything else  lake's own exit code — a real build failure, passed through
    54	#
    55	# `--seed-refresh` rsyncs the primary checkout to chsh and rebuilds the seed
    56	# (the whole of "step 4" of the 2026-09-12 report).  It takes its own lock,
    57	# runs at most once an hour, and is a no-op while the offload is disabled.

Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:

    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis

| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
|---|---|---|
| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |

`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.

Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
next review re-derives from the new diff.

A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`

`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).

The local translation is:

| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
|---|---|---|
| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |

`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.

The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
survives as a lint in all three scripts.

`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
session used one anyway.

The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).

    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch

Issue #505 retired lease-backed native review. Before running a current review,
remove any legacy shell exports so they cannot be mistaken for active routing:

    unset MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_ROOT MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_AUTHORS

Every new code or prose review runs through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` and the
worker-cap reservations in `sessions.md`.

Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
neither publishes a review.

Artefacts:

| Path | Committed | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/blueprint-citations.md` | no | bounded, sanitized label-derived blueprint spans |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/blueprint-citations.raw.md` | no | complete resolver output retained locally |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |

Every current codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, so
the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
(`local/protocols/sessions.md`). A missing dispatcher fails closed. `dispatch.sh` enforces
`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
agreeing is intentional redundancy.

### Historical native review transport (retired by #505)

The remainder of this subsection records the former transport for interpreting
archived requests. It is not an operating procedure: `native_review.py` now
rejects lease-backed roots, and current reviews use external dispatch as described
above.

Before retirement, with external admission held at zero, main could set
`MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_ROOT` and `MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_AUTHORS` (all author
thread IDs, comma-separated).
The unchanged trusted `review.sh` prepares separate code/prose prompts only after
green exact-head CI. `native_review.py request` creates a nonce-bound request under
`CACHE/native-reviews`; main assigns an independent child a fresh turn to read the
entire referenced trusted prompt and review the pinned worktree. The child includes
`Native review binding: NONCE HEAD PROMPT_SHA256` as a separate line before the
normal final `VERDICT` line. Existing independent reviewers may revalidate on a new
parent-assigned turn after request creation; an old completion alone is insufficient.

After the child actually completes, the operator calls
`native_review.py complete REQUEST_JSON CHILD_THREAD`. Both producer and waiting
consumer re-read the canonical live root's rollout, verify direct parentage,
independence, fresh assignment/current-turn completion and the request's recorded
routine/hard model decision with Ultra, including every bound-turn model context
(a final context cannot conceal an earlier different model),
prompt digest and exact worktree head. The mailbox supplies only identity; its
verdict text is never trusted. Fork-inherited parent completions cannot qualify.
Normal `review.sh` parsing, review ledger, exact-head COMMENT/status publication,
kill switches, round cap and merge ownership remain unchanged. A timed-out
observation does not prove the child stopped: inspect its live handle before reuse
or restart. Review transport deployment itself still needs independent review.

A terminated publisher may be continued with
`review.sh PR --resume-native-request CODE_REQUEST_JSON`. A diff touching
`blueprint/` also requires `--resume-native-prose-request PROSE_REQUEST_JSON`;
the two requests must be distinct and both completed lanes must validate.
A prose request is rejected when the diff does not touch `blueprint/`. The command creates
no nonce and invokes no model. It takes the ordinary per-PR review lock without
waiting; a live publisher is a conflict, while a dead holder is reclaimed by the
existing stale-lock rule. Under that lock it rechecks green exact-head CI, the
round cap, the absence of an exact-head review and `local-review/summary`, the
current clean worktree, and the final head before publication.

300	cache, a hardlink build seed and a checkout mirroring this one. ghz reaches it
   301	at 86.7 MB/s over the internal address. A cold lane offload measured 14.9 s and
   302	a one-file rebuild 17.2 s round trip, against 19 minutes for a full warm build
   303	and a 61 s median CI build on a ghz loaded to 90-150 by other users.
   304	
   305	**The owner's rule.** *In full speed mode the compute and the storage of chsh
   306	are used alongside ghz; outside full speed mode chsh is never used.* So the
   307	offload is a property of the run mode and of nothing else:
   308	
   309	```
   310	run_mode.py get offload  ==  yes   iff  run.speed is fast
   311	                                   and  run.compute.offload_hosts lists chsh
   312	                                   and  the run is not paused
   313	```
   314	
   315	Every other case — a default-speed run, a brief that does not list the host, a
   316	paused run, an unreadable run mode, a run-mode document written before the
   317	field existed — is `no`. There is no operator switch, no environment variable
   318	that turns it *on*, and no file an agent can touch to enable it;
   319	`MIPSTARRE_OFFLOAD=0` can only turn it further off. `run_mode.py get
   320	offload_reason` prints the sentence that decided it. `local/bin/offload-build.sh`
   321	asks the run mode itself **before** it honours `MIPSTARRE_OFFLOAD_SCRIPT`, so
   322	that variable can only ever point the offload at a different script — a script
   323	whose `--check` exits 0 still offloads nothing outside full speed mode.
   324	
   325	**And no codex on chsh.** chsh's own internet is about 16 KB/s. It is a pure
   326	build node fed from ghz by rsync: no worker session, no dispatch, no review, no
   327	`codex` installation, ever. Nothing in this layer starts one there.
   328	
   329	**What uses it.** `local/bin/lane.sh` (the pre-push build and the changed-module
   330	build) and `local/bin/ci.sh` (the `local-ci/build` step) take their `lake build`
   331	through `local/bin/offload-build.sh`, which calls
   332	`results/telemetry/owner-tools/build-on-chsh.sh`. That script pushes the
   333	worktree's sources (never `.lake`, `.git`, `.worktrees` or `results/telemetry`),
   334	seeds the lane's `.lake/build` from the shared seed with `cp -al`, points
   335	`.lake/packages` at the shared Mathlib cache, builds, and returns only the
   336	whole `.lake/build` closure. **The pre-push per-file `lake env lean` gate stays
   337	on ghz**, as does everything else that decides whether a branch may be
   338	published: only the compilation moves.
   339	
   340	**chsh is down: there is nothing to do.** Any ssh or rsync failure — an
   341	unreachable host, missing host keys, a busy lane, a toolchain mismatch, a failed
   342	artifact return — exits 64 or 65, and the caller then builds here. A lane never
   343	fails because chsh is unreachable, and a run needs no intervention when it
   344	happens; the lane log says which host built. A build that *failed* is a
   345	different thing and is passed through unchanged: a proof that does not compile
   346	on chsh does not compile here either, and a silent local retry would only spend
   347	the machine's single full-build lease twice. A completed remote exit 124 remains
   348	that build's verdict; only expiry of the outer transport deadline falls back.
   349	
   350	Remote package, seed and retained lane reuse is identity-gated. The package key
   351	comes from `lake-manifest.json` and `lean-toolchain`; the build key also includes
   352	`lakefile.toml`. Seed and lane identity is published only after a successful
   353	build. Missing or incompatible identity exits 64 and uses the existing local
   354	fallback; it never provisions dependencies remotely.
   355	
   356	**How to verify that it was used.**
   357	
   358	```bash
   359	tail ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/chsh/offload.log   # one row per build, naming the host
   360	grep '^offload: ' ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/lanes/<N>.build.log
   361	local/bin/run_mode.py get offload_reason
   362	results/telemetry/owner-tools/build-on-chsh.sh --dry-run <worktree>   # the plan, contacting nothing
   363	```
   364	
   365	A row reading `host=ghz reason=fallback-64` is the farm being unreachable and
   366	the fallback working, not an incident. A run at `fast` speed whose log has no
   367	`host=chsh` row at all is the thing to look at: check `get offload_reason`
   368	first, then the known-hosts file below.
   369	
   370	**The seed.** chsh's checkout and its hardlink seed go stale as `main` moves.
   371	Lanes refuse a seed whose successful-build identity does not match the worktree.
   372	The merge daemon fires `build-on-chsh.sh --seed-refresh` after every merge; the
   373	refresh is detached, takes its own lock, runs at most once an hour and returns
   374	immediately while the offload is disabled. Its log is
   375	`watchdog/chsh/seed-refresh.log`. The rate-limit stamp is written **after** the
   376	rebuild succeeds, so a refresh that fails does not rate-limit its own retries for
   377	an hour.
   378	
   379	`install.sh --start-loops` (run-start step 2) fires one detached
   380	`--seed-refresh` of its own, because the merge daemon only refreshes *after* a
   381	merge: chsh's checkout is at whatever the last run left it. It is a no-op while
   382	the offload is disabled.
   383	
   384	The seed is replaced **in place** (`rsync -a --delete` into the seed directory)
   385	under `seed-refresh.lock`. Lanes take that lock shared while validating identity
   386	and taking the hardlink skeleton, so they cannot reuse a half-replaced seed.
   387	
   388	**Installation.** `results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh` deploys
   389	`build-on-chsh.sh` under the hash manifest like every other operator tool, and
   390	copies the host keys to `watchdog/chsh/known_hosts` (from
   391	`$MIPSTARRE_CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS`, then its own durable copy at
   392	`watchdog/chsh/known_hosts.source`). Shared temporary files are ignored. The
   393	first explicit install keeps that durable copy, and `install.sh --verify`
   394	reports a missing or empty `known_hosts` rather than
   395	leaving the *absence* of `host=chsh` rows as the only signal. The keys
   396	are runtime state, never committed, and the connection is
   397	`StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` against that file: a missing file makes the offload
   398	unusable — which costs a little build time and nothing else — and is never a
   399	reason to accept an unknown host key. Nothing is installed on chsh.
   400	
   401	## 6. Pause and resume
   402	
   403	The owner's word starts the deadline in `run.pause_deadline_min`. The procedure
   404	is one tracked script, `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-pause.sh`, which
   405	ends admission and hands the rest to the standing duties:
   406	
   407	| T | Phase |
   408	|---|---|
   409	| +0:00 | `run_mode.py pause` — caps to 0, the pre-pause caps saved **inside the run mode**, `watchdog/drain` touched |
   410	| +0:30 | queued dispatches release themselves on `watchdog/drain`; keeper, merge daemon and stack-watch stopped by their stop files |

    88	## 3. The cache key
    89	
    90	```
    91	keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
    92	```
    93	
    94	concatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local
    95	analog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in
    96	`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`
    97	and `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay
    98	byte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.
    99	A missing input file is a hard error, never a default.
   100	
   101	Two properties matter, and they are not symmetric:
   102	
   103	1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's
   104	   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest
   105	   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is
   106	   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash
   107	   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not
   108	   need their timestamps preserved.
   109	2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,
   110	   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.
   111	   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`
   112	   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls
   113	   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.

   122	Blueprint citations in Lean docstrings store stable LaTeX labels rather than
   123	numeric blueprint line ranges. Before dispatch, `review.sh` reads
   124	`scripts/blueprint_citations.py` and its TeX helper from the committed trusted
   125	ref, applies them to the reviewed worktree as untrusted data, and attaches
   126	`blueprint-citations.md`. That map derives each cited label's current file and
   127	statement/proof span. A uniquely resolved label suppresses locator-drift
   128	findings; an unknown, duplicate, or mathematically incorrect label does not.
   129	The branch-derived map is sanitized and truncated to
   130	`MIPSTARRE_CITATION_MAX_BYTES` (default 30000) with an explicit marker. It is
   131	attached before the diff in both dispatch paths, reserving its own share of the
   132	dispatcher's aggregate attachment budget. When the map exceeds that budget,
   133	resolved rows are truncated first; every unknown or duplicate-label row is
   134	retained, and review fails closed if those rows themselves cannot fit. The
   135	direct-execution fallback receives this same bounded artifact rather than the
   136	raw resolver output.
   137	The rewrite subcommand exists for the one-time legacy migration, but review
   138	never rewrites the branch.
   139	
   140	## 5. The ping-pong guard
   141	
   142	Three interlocking guards stop a review → fix → review cascade.  All three must
   143	hold; each alone is insufficient.
   144	
   145	1. **Bot-commit skip (here).**  If the head commit's subject matches
   146	   `^\[(claude|codex)-(auto|review)-fix\]`, no review runs.  The regex is
   147	   `pr-review.yml:79` verbatim, and it recognises both providers and both fix
   148	   kinds.  `local/bin/autofix.sh` writes exactly `[codex-auto-fix]` and
   149	   `[codex-review-fix]` (DESIGN.md, "Fix commits").  Change either side without
   150	   the other and this guard fails open, silently.
   151	2. **The combined iteration cap (`autofix.md` §5).**  One counter across all
   152	   fix kinds, not one per kind.
   153	3. **The exclusion of sync and audit failures from auto-fix**
   154	   (`autofix.md` §3).
   155	
   156	The guard has one deliberate hole.  `pr-review.yml:69-72` says: *we only want
   157	to review human-authored pushes and the final bot-fix result (detected by
   158	iteration cap)*.  Without that exception, the last fix commit — the one that
   159	ships — is the only commit on the branch nobody ever reviewed.  So `autofix.sh`
   160	calls `review.sh <id> --force-review` once when the cap is reached — after
   161	**releasing its own fix lock** (`release_fix_lock` in `autofix.sh`), because
   162	`review.sh` refuses to run while the branch's fix lock has a live holder and
   163	that holder would otherwise be the very process asking for the review.
   164	`--force-review` is the only way past rung 7.  Do not use it to "just get a
   165	review" of a bot commit; that reopens the cascade one commit at a time.
   166	
   167	## 6. What the reviewer must return
   168	
   169	A single account cannot approve its own pull request, so GitHub's review-state
   170	field carries no authority here (`issues-prs.md` §2): the verdict is a trailer
   171	in the agent's last message (`codex exec -o <file>`), and the contract demands
   172	three things in order:
   173	
   174	1. a `## Findings` section, one line per finding, in exactly this shape:
   175	
   176	       - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Path/File.lean:123` — one-line summary
   177	
   178	   with severity in {`blocker`, `changes`, `advisory`} and `-` in place of
   179	   `path:line` when a finding is not tied to a line; or the single line
   180	   `- none`;
   181	2. a `## Review` section with the prose;
   182	3. as the final line, alone:
   183	
   184	       VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED
   185	
   186	A missing or malformed trailer is **not** an approval: `review.sh` exits 4,
   187	posts a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and keeps the raw output under
   188	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/`.  Nothing in the findings section

   190	`changes`-severity finding labelled `unparsed finding:`, and a non-approving
   191	verdict with an empty ledger gets one synthesised finding so the merge gate
   192	still blocks.  Both rules follow the same principle as rung 5: the failure mode

   251	
   252	## 9. The findings ledger
   253	
   254	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   255	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   256	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   257	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   258	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   259	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   260	
   261	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   262	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   263	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   264	
   265	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   266	
   267	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   268	|---|---|---|
   269	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   270	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   271	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   272	
   273	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   274	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   275	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   276	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   277	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   278	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   279	
   280	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   281	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   282	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   283	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   284	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   285	must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
   286	and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
   287	is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
   288	decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
   289	without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
   290	repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
   291	A PR that touches only the workflow layer (`local/`, `.githooks/`,
   292	`scripts/tests/`, `docs/`, telemetry) is adjudicated after its SECOND round
   293	because reviewer rounds on scaffolding did not converge (events.md
   294	2026-09-03); a further review is still permitted when the head changed (an
   295	adjudication needs an exact-head review), but it is churn the owner's
   296	watchdog reports.  Mathematics PRs keep the four-round cap above.
   297	
   298	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   299	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   300	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at

   304	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any

     2	# merge.sh <pr> [--adjudicated] — merge one pull request through the gates.
     3	#
     4	# This is the file the merge daemon calls.  Until 2026-09-12 it was
     5	# /tmp/merge-v2.sh, a path that did not exist in any snapshot while the daemon
     6	# header still named merge.sh; the two names now describe one tracked file
     7	# (full-speed-mode v2 design §7, work item W5, finding MT7).
     8	#
     9	# What it does, and nothing else:
    10	#   1. rebases the local `main` onto github/main when it has drifted ahead,
    11	#      stashing and restoring the working tree around it;
    12	#   2. runs `python3 local/bin/pr_merge.py <pr> [--adjudicated]` — the ONLY
    13	#      merge path, with its seven gates untouched.  This script has no flag
    14	#      that can skip, weaken or fake a gate;
    15	#   3. retries once when CI dirties the primary checkout between the stash and
    16	#      the gate ("local changes would be overwritten by merge", 2026-09-04);
    17	#   4. commits the telemetry the merge produced and syncs the mirror.
    18	#
    19	# Stash conflicts on the append-only telemetry records are resolved by union
    20	# (the same rule W7 installs as a merge driver in .gitattributes): every line
    21	# of HEAD, the working tree and the stash, in that order, de-duplicated.  A
    22	# non-append-only file takes the stash version; untracked files come back from
    23	# the stash's third parent.
    24	#
    25	# Exit status: 0 merged; pr_merge.py's own status otherwise (1 on a failed
    26	# rebase).  Output of the gate run is kept at $CACHE_ROOT/daemon/merge-<pr>.out.

    28	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"

     3	Read this before any other protocol. It governs how the protocols themselves
     4	change, and the telemetry duties that make the project usable as research data.
     5	
     6	## Standing principles
     7	
     8	1. **Protocols are normative until amended.** An agent that finds a protocol
     9	   wrong, ambiguous, or costly does not silently deviate: it follows the
    10	   protocol (or stops), records the friction in
    11	   `results/telemetry/events.md`, and proposes an amendment — a dispatched
    12	   worker proposes it to the operator; the operator amends directly under the
    13	   procedure below, an `events.md` incident being a sufficient trigger.  Owner
    14	   sign-off is needed only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.
    15	2. **Amendments are evidence-driven.** Every change to a file under

    17	   `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` citing its trigger: an `events.md` incident,
    18	   a telemetry observation (e.g. repeated duplicate builds in

    23	   "how should this work?"; deviations are fine when the local setting
    24	   genuinely differs, and must be recorded in `EVOLUTION.md` with the reason.

## Findings
- [ ] F1 (changes) `results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh:114` — The installer leaves legacy active or durable host keys trusted, so upgrading does not remove the unsafe `/tmp` bootstrap.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `results/telemetry/owner-tools/build-on-chsh.sh:262` — The detached seed rebuild ignores `CHSH_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S` and can hold `seed-refresh.lock` indefinitely.

## Review
Prior F1 is resolved by distinguishing a completed exit 124 through the completion marker. Prior F2’s artifact identities and prior F3’s direct resume rollback are also addressed. Prior F4 remains as current F1.

For F1, the previous implementation could promote `/tmp/chsh-setup/known_hosts` into both `known_hosts.source` and the active file. The repaired installer accepts any existing durable copy as trusted; when no source exists, it also returns without deactivating an existing active file. Since `build-on-chsh.sh` checks only readability, an upgrade can continue using the old unsafe trust state. Require explicit rebootstrap or provenance metadata, quarantine legacy files, and add an upgrade-path test.

For F2, ordinary remote builds use `timeout $BUILD_TIMEOUT_S`, but seed refresh runs bare `lake build` while holding the exclusive seed lock. The helper’s outer timeout does not apply because install and the merge daemon invoke seed refresh directly. A live but hung remote build can therefore disable farm reuse indefinitely. Apply the build timeout to this path and test it.

The attached aggregate diff was truncated, so I reviewed the authoritative on-disk patch and checkout. `git diff --check` and `bash -n` passed. The focused unit suite could not be rerun because the read-only sandbox had no writable temporary directory; the task reports exact-head local CI as green.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
